pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: src/lib/mcp/work-tools.ts:362 The MCP work protocol (claim under a lease, brief, report) runs remote agents as a pull-queue fleet, but report_attempt accepts a report that carries no fence, so a superseded session on the same token can still write into a newer claim. That is exactly the 'late finished signal races a lost verdict' case session-registry exists to close; only an explicitly stale fence is refused.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/mcp/work-tools.ts:362 The fence (claim generation) is optional and only logged as deprecated, so a fence-less late report from an earlier session of the same holder is accepted.
src/lib/mcp/tools.ts:150 Executors pull work through the authenticated MCP door and run it in their own harness. Ascent executes nothing and needs no ingress to them.
src/lib/mcp/tools.ts:21 A delegate's 'resolved' is only an account. Done is decided server-side by a default-branch rescan that measures the dimension moving.
src/lib/mcp/work-tools.ts:305 Each brief carries the org's standard, autonomy tier, review text, human-review requirement, lease and stance, and admission is re-checked when the brief is issued.

src/lib/mcp/work-tools.ts:350 Each per-row report passes one validation door (closed verdict enum, required reason), and skipped/needs_human make failure a first-class result. Roster-level accounting is not in this context.

pairs.registryProposal: session-registry could name the transitional case explicitly: a generation fence added as optional for backward compatibility leaves the late-signal race open for fence-less clients until the fence is mandatory.
